title: Dual-Sublattice Ferromagnetism Driven by Cooperative Double Exchange and Superexchange at NdNiO$_3$/CaMnO$_3$ Interfaces
authors: Sharup Sheikh, Uditha M. Jayathilake, Michael Terilli, Mikhail Kareev, Jay R. Paudel, Arian Arab, Christoph Klewe, Tien-Lin Lee, Jak Chakhalian, Alexander X. Gray
abstract: Engineering emergent ferromagnetism at correlated-oxide interfaces offers a powerful route to creating collective states that do not exist in the parent materials. Here, we show that interfacial valence reconstruction in NdNiO$_3$/CaMnO$_3$ superlattices generates dual-sublattice ferromagnetism involving both Mn and Ni. Depth-resolved standing-wave X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals enhanced Mn$^{3+}$ character on the CaMnO$_3$ side of the interface and enhanced Ni$^{2+}$ character on the NdNiO$_3$ side, establishing the configurations required for Mn$^{4+}$-O-Mn$^{3+}$ double exchange and Ni$^{2+}$-O-Mn$^{4+}$ superexchange, respectively. At low temperature, element-specific XMCD reveals ferromagnetic responses from both sublattices, with the Ni response concentrated predominantly in the Ni$^{2+}$-derived spectral component that SW-XPS independently shows to be enhanced at the interface. Together, these results show that cooperative double exchange within CaMnO$_3$ and superexchange across the interface couple the Mn and Ni sublattices, providing a general strategy for engineering interfacial ferromagnetism in correlated oxides.
summary: This paper investigates how to induce ferromagnetism at the interface of $	ext{NdNiO}_3/	ext{CaMnO}_3$ superlattices. Using advanced X-ray spectroscopies, the authors prove that interfacial valence reconstruction creates the necessary conditions—specifically, $	ext{Mn}^{3+}$ and $	ext{Ni}^{2+}$—to activate cooperative double exchange and superexchange. This coupling mechanism successfully engineers a robust, dual-sublattice ferromagnetism.
main_problem: The study aims to understand how to engineer emergent ferromagnetism at the interface between correlated oxides by controlling the electronic structure.
main_result: The research demonstrates that interfacial valence reconstruction, specifically enhanced $	ext{Mn}^{3+}$ and $	ext{Ni}^{2+}$ character, activates cooperative double exchange and superexchange pathways, leading to dual-sublattice ferromagnetism.
method: The study employs depth-resolved Standing-Wave X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (SW-XPS) to map valence states and X-ray Magnetic Circular Dichroism (XMCD) to measure magnetic responses.
model_or_system: The physical system is an epitaxial superlattice of $	ext{NdNiO}_3/	ext{CaMnO}_3$. The mechanism relies on the interplay between charge transfer, valence state reconstruction, and magnetic exchange interactions (double exchange and superexchange) at the heterointerface.
key_observables: Interfacial $	ext{Mn}^{3+}$ and $	ext{Ni}^{2+}$ enhancement (via SW-XPS); Ferromagnetic response from both Mn and Ni sublattices (via XMCD).
important_parameters: Low temperature ($20 	ext{ K}$); Specific incidence angles for depth profiling; The ratio of $	ext{Mn}^{3+}/	ext{Mn}^{4+}$ and $	ext{Ni}^{2+}/	ext{Total Ni}$.
main_assumptions: The ability to distinguish interfacial vs. layer-interior electronic states using the standing-wave electric field profile is crucial for the analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SW-XPS geometry and depth-selective measurements, showing valence profiles (Mn and Ni) and the resulting XMCD signals confirming magnetic coupling.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the structural and chemical composition using RHEED/HAXPES, then uses SW-XPS to map the necessary interfacial valence reconstruction ($	ext{Mn}^{3+}$ and $	ext{Ni}^{2+}$), and finally uses XMCD to confirm the resulting dual-sublattice ferromagnetism driven by the identified exchange mechanisms.
why_interesting: This work provides a clear, experimentally validated blueprint for designing magnetic properties in artificial quantum materials by engineering the local electronic structure at interfaces, which is highly relevant to correlated electron physics.
